{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}
The [Financial Plan](../economics/financial-plan.qmd) describes raising {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}}, spending it, and managing {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year forever. The [Roadmap](../strategy/roadmap.qmd) describes the phases. This chapter describes the part that comes before all of that: the $1M-3M it takes to build the organization that does those things.

On Wishonia, when we wanted to redirect resources from destruction to medicine, the whole setup took about a week. On Earth, you need to incorporate four legal entities, hire three specialists, and build a "data room," which is not a room and does not contain data in any physical sense. It's a folder. Your species charges $50,000 in legal fees to create a folder.

## Phase 0: Build the Machine That Builds the Machine

Your [Legal Architecture](../legal/legal-framework.qmd) describes four entities: the Brain (501(c)(3)), the Sword (501(c)(4)), the Engine (Victory Corporation), and the Soul (DIH Foundation). You don't need all four on day one. You need two.

### Immediate Incorporations

**Victory Corporation (the Engine):** A Delaware C-Corp that will issue [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd), hire the core team, raise capital, and eventually administer the treaty's 20% non-medical allocation on treaty inflows ({{< var victory_bond_funding_pct >}} to investor dividends, {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} to political incentives). The company runs the treasury infrastructure; it does not get unilateral discretion over those percentages. This is the entity that does things. All initial hires are employees of this entity.

**DIH Foundation (the Soul):** A Swiss nonprofit that owns 100% of Victory Corporation. Its charter is permanently locked to ending war and disease, which means no future board can decide the real mission was luxury condos all along. You incorporate this first or simultaneously, because a for-profit corporation without a nonprofit leash is just a corporation, and your species has enough of those.

The other two entities (501(c)(3) Brain, 501(c)(4) Sword) come later, when you need tax-deductible donations and political lobbying infrastructure. For now, you need a company that can hire people and a foundation that can stop the company from becoming evil. That's the minimum viable legal structure.

## The Pre-Seed Round: $1M-3M

This is not the {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} bond raise. This is startup capital to fund the company that will organize the bond raise. The distinction matters because investors in this round are betting on the team, not the treaty. They're funding the construction of the machine, not the machine's output.

| Use | Allocation | Purpose |
|-----|-----------|---------|
| Salaries | 50-60% | Founder + 3 activation team hires for 12-18 months |
| Legal & Compliance | 20-25% | Securities counsel, election law, international treaty frameworks |
| Platform Prototyping | 10-15% | Early architecture of the global referendum platform |
| Operations | 5-10% | Office, technology, establishment of the data room (the expensive folder) |

Victory Corporation raises this round. Standard venture terms. The investors in this round get equity in the corporation that will later issue the bonds, manage the treasury infrastructure, and administer the treaty's 20% non-medical allocation on {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}}/year in treaty inflows. Their upside is the upside of the company that runs the infrastructure, not a direct claim on treaty flows (that's what the bonds are for).

## The Activation Team: Three Hires

Your species has a saying: "you can't boil the ocean." This is correct. You can, however, hire three people who know how to build a machine that boils the ocean. The three immediate hires, detailed in the [Hiring Plan](careers/hiring-plan.qmd):

### 1. Capital Markets Lead

Structures the VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds, builds the financial model and data room, and leads the Seed and Series A fundraising. This person has spent their career turning complicated financial ideas into documents that make rich people comfortable parting with money. On Wishonia, we don't need this role because we don't have rich people. On Earth, this is your most important hire.

### 2. Elections & IE Compliance Lead

Designs the legally compliant framework for the [global referendum](../strategy/global-referendum.qmd) and the multi-jurisdictional independent expenditure strategy. This person understands the difference between "lobbying" (legal), "campaign contributions" (legal), "independent expenditures" (legal), and "bribery" (illegal but identical to the previous three except for the paperwork). On your planet, this distinction determines whether you go to prison or get a tax deduction.

### 3. Growth & Referrals Lead

Designs the technology, incentive structure, and viral referral mechanics of the global referendum platform. This person's job is to make clicking "I prefer not dying" as contagious as clicking "I prefer this dance video." The referendum needs {{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target_nounit >}} participants. Getting there at $0.50-0.89 per vote instead of $5-15 per vote is the difference between a {{< var treaty_campaign_viral_referendum_base_case >}} referendum budget and a $4B referendum budget. This hire is the reason the first number is possible.

## What Success Looks Like

Phase 0 is complete when:

1. Victory Corporation and DIH Foundation are legally incorporated
2. $1M-3M is raised and deployed
3. Three activation team members are hired and working
4. The financial model and data room are ready for the Seed round ($250-400M)
5. The referendum platform has a working prototype
6. Legal frameworks for securities (Reg D) and election law (IE compliance) are in place

At that point, you're ready for the [Financial Plan](../economics/financial-plan.qmd)'s Seed phase. Everything before this is building the launchpad. Everything after is the launch.
